critique: The black background and pink-lilac glow are directionally appropriate, and t4 contains more individual soft blob forms than the prior render. However, the result still reads as a small central firework: bright sharp radial streaks and a dense white-hot core dominate both frames, while the t1-to-t4 change is an abrupt outward burst. The intended look needs a much broader, airier field of independently soft luminous blobs with gentle drift rather than an exploding, center-originating cluster.

suggestions.why: Disable the auxiliary particle emission that is contributing conspicuous sharp streaks around the otherwise soft blobs.
Greatly reduce main-particle velocity so the t1-to-t4 evolution reads as gentle drift rather than a radial explosion.
Widen the emitter substantially to distribute blobs across a broader horizontal field instead of concentrating them in the center.
Expand the vertical emission area as well, producing the airy scattered blob composition indicated by the preset thumbnail.
